newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grisly final chapter in German kidnap case.
newsitem.headline: Grisly final chapter in German kidnap case.

text.p: A body found in woodland outside Frankfurt was formally identified on Sunday as that of a kidnapped multi-millionaire, bringing a gruesome end to a three-week saga which has horrified Germany.
Police with dogs found a partly decomposed corpse lying face down under a patch of leaves and a felled pine tree on Saturday.
They said on Sunday that tests confirmed the body was that of 40-year-old Jakub Fiszman, owner of an electronics and property empire, who was abducted outside his Frankfurt office on October 1.
"A DNA analysis on the body tissue has positively identified the corpse to be that of Jakub Fiszman," police said in a brief statement.
Police imposed a news blackout after the kidnapping.

But they appealed to the public for help some two weeks later when abductors reneged on a promise to free Fiszman, best known for financing the failed Frankfurt production of the rock musical "Tommy". His brother had paid a four million mark ($2.50 million) ransom.

Police made rapid progress after going public, arresting two people -- Rainer Koerppen, 48, and his 26-year old son Sven -- within a few days and discovering almost all of the ransom in the garden of a house owned by Rainer Koerppen's parents.

Their search for Fiszman, whose family fortune has been valued at over 400 million marks but who largely kept out of the public eye, concentrated on countryside and woodland in the Taunus region about 50km (30 miles) outside Frankfurt.

Tornado reconnaisance jets with heat-seeking equipment were brought in to scan the area and hundreds of police officers combed the woods for clues. As the hunt went on, police grew more pessimistic about the fate of the missing man.
The last sign he was alive came the day after his abduction when he phoned a friend to relay the kidnappers' demands.

Last Friday, Sven Koerppen told police he and his father drove Fiszman to the Taunus area on October 4 -- just three days after he was kidnapped. According to the son's testimony his father went into the woods with Fiszman and returned alone.
Police have said no exact cause and time of death has been established but said the victim suffered considerable blows. The body may have lain in the same spot for a number of weeks.

Several wealthy Germans, including Fiszman's nephew in 1991, have been abducted in recent years, but they were usually released unharmed. The grisly details of this abduction and its tragic conclusion have left a deeper impression.
Police said the son had told them his father's mask had slipped off during an initial scuffle when they kidnapped Fiszman, enabling the victim to catch a glimpse of his captor.
That short glimpse may have been the reason Fiszman was killed, police said. Rainer Koerppen has denied any involvement in the kidnapping.
Police were also looking for at least one other kidnapper believed to have been in involved in making the ransom demands.
